title: Pinball Workshop
description: Design a pinball table part by part, then play it with real flipper physics — and share the whole table in a link.
concept: A two-mode pinball machine: Design mode gives you a toolbox of bumpers, pegs, kickers, drop targets, spinners and drag-drawn walls that you place on a 420x720 playfield; Play mode drops three balls down a plunger lane into whatever you built. The physics is a sub-stepped impulse solver — circle and segment collisions with per-part restitution, flippers that impart true surface velocity from their angular speed, nudge with a tilt meter, and a ball-search kick that frees a ball trapped in a pocket. Four built-in tables ship with it; your own tables save to the browser, export as JSON, and pack into a share URL.
features: Design mode: 6 part types, drag-to-draw walls, move/erase tools, grid snap and a one-tap mirror
Play mode: 3 balls, scoring, spinner-driven multiplier, drop targets, nudge with tilt penalty
Angular-velocity flippers on keyboard (A/L, arrows) or bottom-screen touch pads
Live physics sliders — gravity, bounce and flipper kick — plus three themes and a ball trail
Per-table high scores and a saved table library in localStorage
Export the table as .json, snapshot the playfield as .png, or copy a share link that encodes the whole layout

interaction.mouse: In Design mode, drag parts to reposition them and drag to draw walls; sliders retune the physics live.
interaction.click: Pick a part from the toolbox and click the playfield to drop it; click the table in Play mode to launch a ball.
interaction.touch: Tap the bottom-left or bottom-right of the screen for the flippers; the gear button opens the tool sheet.
interaction.keyboard: A / ← left flipper, L / → right flipper, Space to launch, N to nudge.
